entries.label: To the One with the Light
Menu confirmation cue
entries.description: Used when accepting a map-menu action with A. Plays a sound sequence; it does not change the music volume. Its sound depends on the loaded sound bank.
entries.evidence: Use verified in native menu code; exact sound-bank identity is not independently named.

entries.label: Dialogue text blip (variant 3)
entries.description: The dialogue text-sound routine uses this cue for text-sound setting 3. This is a text/voice blip, not a music fade. Its sound depends on the loaded bank.

entries.label: Menu cancel / back cue
entries.description: Used when backing out of a map-menu action with B. Plays a sound sequence without changing the music volume; its sound depends on the loaded bank.
entries.evidence: Use verified in native menu code; exact sound-bank identity is not independently named.

entries.label: Music synchronization signal
entries.description: Sets an audio-driver synchronization flag, which a waiting music sequence can check. It does not select a track or perform a fade. The precise audible cue affected in each scene is not fully verified.
entries.evidence: Flag write and sequence wait check verified in SPC code; scene-specific musical purpose remains partly understood.

entries.label: Fade out / stop music (~0.5 s)
entries.description: Fades music volume to zero over 31 driver ticks (about 0.5 seconds in the preview), then stops the current music sequence. $00E0 is fastest; $00E7 is slowest. To hear music again after completion, use Play Song; $00E8 alone does not restart the stopped track.
entries.evidence: SPC fade handler, countdown and stopped-sequence traces verified. Times are approximate and specific to the native driver.

entries.label: Restore music volume (~0.5 s)
entries.description: Fades music volume up to its full internal level of 255 over 31 driver ticks (about 0.5 seconds in the preview). It restores music ducked by $00F7 / $7FF7. It does not choose a track or restart music already stopped by a completed fade-out.
entries.evidence: SPC handler and volume traces verified; native village scripts pair $7FF7 with $00E8.
entries.preview_note: With background music selected, the preview first reduces its volume so this restoration can be heard.

entries.label: Duck music to 60/255 (~24%)
entries.description: Fades music volume to internal level 60 over 24 driver ticks (about 0.4 seconds), leaving the track running. With a zero high byte, the driver uses 60 as its default target. $00E8 restores full volume.
entries.evidence: SPC parameter handler and final-volume trace verified.

entries.label: Duck music to 127/255 (~50%)
entries.description: Fades music volume to internal level 127 over 24 driver ticks (about 0.4 seconds), leaving the track running. The high byte $7F supplies the target level: this is not interchangeable with $00F7. Commonly used to lower background music during village dialogue/rewards; $00E8 restores it.
entries.evidence: SPC high-byte parameter handling, native village call sites and final-volume trace verified.
